newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - March 5.

text.p: The government would budget to spend an extra $950 million this year, Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday -- $250 million less than promised in the Coalition agreement. However, Peters said the government remained committed to implementing all its promises, which would mean spending an extra $5 billion during three years. "We will spend what needs to be spent to get our most important initiatives working," Peters said. Page 1.

The Winebox inquiry was accused of letting Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters off the hook, during criticism by lawyers for European Pacific and Fay Richwhite. Richard Craddock, QC, for European Pacific, said in his opening address on Tuesday that the inquiry had a "closed mind", and that counsel assisting the inquiry, Colin Carruthers, QC, had assumed the role of Peters. Page 1.

Laws governing trout fishing should apply to all New Zealanders, Attorney-General Paul East said on Tuesday. East said his telephone had been running hot with calls from concerned anglers since last week when a judge found a man from a Wanganui tribe not guilty of fishing without a licence. East said the decision was of considerable concern to all people who enjoyed recreational trout fishing. Page 2.

NZ First MP Tukoirangi Morgan called on Tuesday for Alliance deputy leader Sandra Lee to give up her place on the Maori affairs select committee. Morgan, who renounced last month his hopes of chairing the committee, said Lee should give up her place to fellow Alliance MP Alamein Kopu. Kopu is the only Alliance MP not to have a place on any of Parliament's 17 select committees. Page 2.

Parliament began an angry debate on Tuesday about the formation of select committees, caused by a dispute between the government and Labour over which MPs should chair the committees. Select committees, vital to Parliament's work in scrutinising legislation and hearing public submissions, should have been set up soon after the election but the row has dragged on and on Tuesday it moved into the debating chamber. Page 2.

Treasury advised the government not to pay for costs incurred by political parties seeking advice during the post-election coalition negotiations, Treasury papers have shown. Papers made public under the Official Information Act show that on October 25 last year, Treasury told Finance Minister Bill Birch that it considered that parties were already adequately funded and that "in our opinion, the commission of independent advice is part of the routine management of a political party". Page 2.

The government budget policy statement issued on Tuesday was generally in line with market expectations, even though spending will be $250 million less than expected in the coming financial year. The lower spending in the coming year will allow the phasing in of new programmes and will be made up in the third year out. The change was seen as a timing matter and so had little or no effect on the financial markets. Page 8.

Ergo Personal Financial Services has become the first financial institution to sign an agreement with NZ Post allowing its customers to deposit money at Post Shops. The agency agreement allows Ergo customers to open term deposit and call accounts at Post Shops from March 10. Ergo is AMP's direct banking subsidiary, launched in 1995. It offers a range of home loans, and savings and investment products over the phone. Page 8.

Owning part of a hotel that pools returns to share out equally to titleholders is the latest investment opportunity in New Zealand. A prospectus was issued in Auckland on Tuesday for unit title ownership of the 268-suite Auckland Habour Travelodge Hotel which will be built by 1999 on lower Albert Street in central Auckland. Page 8.

Retirement home operator Metropolitan Life Care has announced a rise in annual bottom-line profit to $3.3 million in the year to December from $531,000 last year. The profit was achieved on total operating revenue of $34.7 million, up 38 percent from $26,97 million and sales revenue from the second half was $20.5 million against $14.5 million last year. Page 8.
